run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:21:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy genuinely emitted error traffic in the window. Its own 'ingress' spans on service_name="frontend-proxy" carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR: 5m increase was 0 at 05:20:22, 1.25 at 05:22:22, 67.78 at 05:24:22 and 05:26:22, 25.56 at 05:28:22, with earlier background levels of 1.48-7.78 per 5m. Its access log shows two distinct classes. (a) A background class of HTTP 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' from upstream 'frontend', present throughout 05:20-05:30 (e.g. 05:20:44, 05:23:13, 05:26:02, 05:28:27, 05:30:09); the 5m error window ending 05:20:22 was 0 and a 503 was logged at 05:20:44, immediately before the alert label time 05:21:22. (b) A distinct surge of HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout from 05:21:45.322Z to 05:23:25.071Z, matching checkout's own ERROR spans on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (44 errors in 05:23-05:24, 0 before and after 05:10-05:40) and frontend's ERROR spans on POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (74 errors 05:22-05:23, 44 in 05:23-05:24). That surge is explained by Deployment otel-demo/payment being rolled at 05:21:39: a new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 whose pod template differs from payment-55766d76b9 only by annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:21:39Z (empty spec diff); the only payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was killed at 05:21:42 and the replacement container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 05:22:53.877Z, while its container has no readinessProbe and the Deployment runs one replica. The first checkout 500 is 3 s after the kill and 68 s before the gRPC server started, and the 500s stop at 05:23:25 as payment began completing charges at 05:23:31. Payment itself shows zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and healthy 'Transaction complete.' logs, so it was rolled out, not damaged. What remains unresolved: the exact alerting expression (no Alertmanager rules loaded), the frontend container's own logs (0 lines readable), Jaeger spans after ~05:08:23, and therefore the origin of the chronic 503/connection-termination class that the alert most plausibly reflects at its 05:21:22 start.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span metrics show STATUS_CODE_ERROR on span_name 'ingress': increase over 5m was 0 at 05:20:22, 1.25 at 05:22:22, 67.78 at 05:24:22, 67.78 at 05:26:22, 25.56 at 05:28:22 and 2.22 at 05:30:22; the sibling series span_name 'router frontend egress' with STATUS_CODE_ERROR tracks it (65.56 at 05:24:22 and 05:26:22, 22.22 at 05:28:22). Background error levels earlier in the window were 1.48-7.78 per 5m.

frontend-proxy's access log records HTTP 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' from upstream 'frontend' for varied routes (GET /api/recommendations at 05:20:44, GET /api/products at 05:23:13 and 05:24:12, GET /api/products at 05:26:02, GET /api/products at 05:28:27, GET /api/cart at 05:30:09), i.e. the frontend side terminated the connection before a response started.

Sampled traces from 05:02-05:08 show the same shape: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with http.status_code 503 / otel.status_code ERROR and a matching frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' span with error="true", http.status_code="0" and no visible frontend child span, while the load-generator GET span in the same trace also carries 503/ERROR.

frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500 with response-code-details 'via_upstream' on POST /api/checkout between 05:21:45.322Z and 05:23:25.071Z; the earliest such line is 05:21:45.322Z and there were no /api/checkout 500 lines between 05:15:00 and 05:21:45.

checkout's own ERROR spans are confined to 05:22-05:24: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge each show 44 error spans in the minute 05:23:00-05:24:00 and 0 in every minute before and after across 05:10-05:40; frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder shows 74 error spans in 05:22:00-05:23:00 and 44 in 05:23:00-05:24:00.

frontend's own ERROR spans in the window are only on the checkout route: 'POST /api/checkout', 'POST', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' show 41.11 error spans at 05:23:00, 65.56 at 05:25:00 and 65.56 at 05:27:00 (5m increases), then 0 at 05:29:00 and later; all other frontend operations (GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, cart and ad gRPC calls, tcp.connect) stayed at 0.

Deployment otel-demo/payment was rolled at 05:21:39: ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 was created at 2026-11-17T05:21:39Z, the Deployment scaled it 0->1 and scaled payment-55766d76b9 1->0 at 05:21:42, ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 reported 'Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4', and pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was 'Killing'/'Stopping container payment' at 05:21:42 while payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht was Scheduled 05:21:39, Created 05:21:41 and Started 05:21:42.

The payment rollout was a restart with an unchanged pod template: the only difference between the pod templates of payment-55766d76b9 and payment-7b6bfb9fb4 is the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:21:39Z (computed spec diff list is empty; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env and resources).

The replacement payment container did not serve until well after it was Started: its first log line is 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 2026-11-17T05:22:53.877Z (71 s after the old pod was killed at 05:21:42), the first 'Charge request received.' is at 05:23:31.929Z, and the container spec has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe while Deployment payment runs 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready replica.

The first frontend-proxy 500 on POST /api/checkout (05:21:45.322Z) is 3 s after the old payment pod was killed (05:21:42) and 68 s before the replacement payment gRPC server started (05:22:53.877Z); the 500s stop at 05:23:25, immediately after payment began completing charges at 05:23:31.929Z.

The payment service itself shows no failure signal: its per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase was 0 across 05:00-05:41:22 while its oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans continued to be recorded, and its logs show repeated 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs from 05:23:31 through 05:29:58.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts and no waiting or last-terminated reason; all 21 otel-demo Deployments are at desired 1 / available 1 / ready 1 with no unavailable replicas; payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht (start 05:21:39) is the only pod whose start time is after 04:50:28.

There are no NetworkPolicies in namespace otel-demo (the query returned an empty list), and every otel-demo Service has endpoints (frontend 100.96.5.113:8080, payment 100.96.5.94:8080, frontend-proxy 100.96.5.200:8080, checkout 100.96.5.42:8080).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines fault-injection flags; the only one not at off/0 is paymentFailure with defaultVariant "100%" (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'), while paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad and emailMemoryLeak are all off/0.

The metric inventory reachable for this target (63 names, incomplete false) contains only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket plus container/JVM/process/redis/v8js and otelcol metrics; the only series carrying service_name="frontend-proxy" are those two traces_span_metrics series, so no HTTP, rpc or kube-state error-rate metric for frontend-proxy is queryable here.

The 05:21:45-05:23:25 error surge observable at frontend-proxy is a downstream consequence of Deployment otel-demo/payment's restartedAt rollout: killing the single payment pod at 05:21:42 while the replacement gRPC server was not listening until 05:22:53 left checkout without a payment backend, so oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls failed (checkout recorded ERROR spans with no corresponding payment server span), checkout PlaceOrder errored, frontend returned HTTP 500 on /api/checkout and frontend-proxy recorded ingress error spans. Consistent with this, payment's Charge span count at 05:25:00 (143.3 per 5m) sits below its ~190 per 5m baseline by roughly the number of failing checkout calls.

The alert label time 05:21:22, before the payment kill, most plausibly reflects the chronic 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' class: the 5-minute error window ending 05:20:22 was 0, a 503 UC was logged at 05:20:44, and a strictly greater-than-zero threshold is met by that single error. The origin of these frontend-side connection terminations is not established by the available evidence.

The flagd-config setting paymentFailure=defaultVariant "100%" is a fault-injection candidate that could explain charge failures, but the evidence does not tie it to this incident: payment logged successful 'Transaction complete.' charges from 05:23:31 while that value is present, payment's own ERROR span increase was 0, and the failing calls coincided with the interval when no payment server was listening.

The data-recorders workload churn (7 Pod Created, 2 FailedScheduling, PVC ExternalProvisioning/WaitForFirstConsumer, PV VolumeFailedDelete) was not the cause of this alert: those events belong to Job/StatefulSet/Deployment objects in namespace data-recorders (clickhouse-unified-recorder, jaeger-traces-recorder, kubernetes-topology-recorder, prometheus-alert-recorder), and the two FailedScheduling messages are VolumeBinding pre-bind retries ('the object has been modified') followed within seconds by successful Scheduled and Started events; no otel-demo error evidence ties to them.

The payment pod was replaced by its own controller, not damaged: ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 reported 'Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4', the new pod's restart count is 0, both ReplicaSets use the same image and container spec, and no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff state appears on any otel-demo pod.

No memory-pressure or CPU-starvation change accompanies the errors: frontend container working set is flat at ~120-129 MB and frontend-proxy at ~20 MB across 05:00-05:36, and the frontend container's CPU-throttling rate stays in a narrow band (2.88, 2.42, 2.16, 2.47, 2.39, 2.38, 1.36 per second at 05:05-05:35) with no spike around 05:20-05:24.

Give the payment container a readinessProbe (and/or run more than one replica) so that a restartedAt rollout cannot terminate the only payment pod before its gRPC server on port 8080 is listening; that gap was the direct mechanism of the checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy error surge.

Confirm whether paymentFailure defaultVariant "100%" in otel-demo/flagd-config is intentional and whether the payment service actually evaluates it; if not, reset it, since a fault-injection flag left at 100% is a latent source of the same error class.

Make the frontend container's stdout/stderr readable through the log path and retain Jaeger history across the whole incident window so that the chronic frontend-side 503 UC connection terminations can be diagnosed rather than remaining an unexplained background error class.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and without a filter both returned nothing (status no_data), so the rule expression, its window and the reported value 0.01111111111111111 (1/90) could not be verified; that query matched nothing and the alerting metric remains unknown.

frontend container logs were not readable through this tool (the query returned 0 lines for frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc in both 05:22-05:26 and 05:15-05:42, status no_data), so the frontend side of the 503 UC 'connection_termination' responses could not be examined.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy in 05:18-05:35 and none for frontend in 05:14-05:42 (status no_data); the newest trace data delivered was ~05:08:23, so trace-level detail of the 05:21-05:24 failure window is missing and that window rests only on aggregated span metrics plus proxy and payment logs.

The trigger of the kubectl rollout restart on Deployment payment at 05:21:39 (who or what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run and no configuration value was shown to cause the restart.
Logs of the terminated payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 were unavailable (previous container instance not found), so its final requests and shutdown behaviour could not be inspected.
The PersistentVolume named by the data-recorders VolumeFailedDelete event was not read; the event exists but the object itself was not inspected, and no otel-demo evidence ties it to this alert.
A query for ResourceQuotas in otel-demo returned nothing (status no_data), so quota exhaustion is neither confirmed nor excluded; it is reported as an unchecked resource rather than a zero value.
Impact outside otel-demo (end-user or customer effect) was not observed; only spans, logs and error counters inside otel-demo were examined.
next_steps: Compare the alert's own metric definition and evaluation timestamp against the traces_span_metrics pipeline, whose freshness was roughly 389-730 s behind wall clock during this Run, to establish whether alert start 05:21:22 was computed from data around 05:15-05:21.
Retrieve retained frontend pod logs or an Envoy upstream-reset trace for 05:20:44 and the other 503 UC timestamps to identify why the frontend closed connections before responding.
Fetch change history or audit records for namespace otel-demo around 05:21:39 to identify who performed the kubectl rollout restart on Deployment payment and why.

Verify at runtime whether the payment service evaluates flagd's paymentFailure flag (currently defaultVariant "100%") and whether checkout uses paymentUnreachable, before treating either as an incident cause.
